nodes.bioSummaryDe: Österreichisch-amerikanischer Ökonom, Begründer der Theorie der schöpferischen Zerstörung und unternehmerischen Innovation.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Austrian-born economist who pioneered the theory of creative destruction and entrepreneurial innovation.
nodes.keyWorks: Theory of Economic Development (1911); Business Cycles (1939); Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy (1942)
nodes.keyContribution: Creative destruction and entrepreneurial innovation
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: Samuelson, Tobin, Tsuru, Heilbroner, Bergson, Metzler; Student of: Bhm-Bawerk, Wieser, Philippovich

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Österreichischer Ökonom mit grundlegenden Beiträgen zur monetären Konjunkturtheorie, der Debatte über sozialistische Wirtschaftsrechnung und der Theorie spontaner Ordnung.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Austrian economist who made fundamental contributions to monetary cycle theory, the socialist calculation debate, and the theory of spontaneous order.
nodes.keyWorks: Prices and Production (1931); The Road to Serfdom (1944); The Constitution of Liberty (1960)
nodes.keyContribution: Spontaneous order and the price system as an information mechanism
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: Hicks, Lerner, Kaldor, Friedrich Lutz, Vera Lutz; Student of: Wieser, Böhm-Bawerk

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Amerikanischer Ökonom, der die Mathematisierung der Wirtschaftswissenschaft vorantrieb und das erfolgreichste Lehrbuch der Volkswirtschaftslehre verfasste.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: American economist who personified mainstream economics in the 20th century, launching the mathematization of economics and writing the most successful principles textbook.
nodes.keyWorks: Foundations of Economic Analysis (1947); Economics: An introductory analysis (1948); Linear Programming and Economic Analysis (1958)
nodes.keyContribution: Mathematization of economics and Neoclassical-Keynesian Synthesis
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: Robert M. Solow; Student of: Joseph Schumpeter, Wassily Leontief, Gottfried Haberler, Alvin Hansen, Edwin Bidwell Wilson

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Führender englischer Ökonom, einer der Hauptvertreter der Neoklassik und Autor der einflussreichen „Principles of Economics".
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Prominent English economist, one of the leading propagators of Neoclassical economics, and author of the successful textbook Principles of Economics.
nodes.keyWorks: Principles of Economics (1890); Industry and Trade (1919); Money, Credit and Commerce (1923)
nodes.keyContribution: Neoclassical theory of value and supply-and-demand diagram
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: Herbert S Foxwell, John Neville Keynes, William Cunningham, John Shield Nicholson, L.L. Price; Student of: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Schottischer Philosoph und Ökonom der Aufklärung, weithin als „Vater der Nationalökonomie" anerkannt.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Scottish philosopher and economist, leading figure of the Scottish Enlightenment, widely regarded as the 'father of economics'.
nodes.keyWorks: The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759); An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776)
nodes.keyContribution: Classical political economy and the Wealth of Nations
nodes.teacherStudent: Student of: Francis Hutcheson; Teacher of: John Millar

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Britisch-niederländischer Wirtschaftswissenschaftler, führender Methodologe und Historiker des ökonomischen Denkens.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Dutch-born British economist known for his extensive work in the history of economic thought and the methodology of economics.
nodes.keyWorks: Ricardian Economics (1958); Economic Theory in Retrospect (1962); The Methodology of Economics (1980)
nodes.keyContribution: History of economic thought and methodology of economics
nodes.teacherStudent: Student of: George Stigler

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Britischer Ökonom, dessen „General Theory" die Makroökonomik revolutionierte und die Wirtschaftspolitik des 20. Jahrhunderts prägte.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: British economist who revolutionized macroeconomics by demonstrating that aggregate demand determines overall economic activity and employment.
nodes.keyWorks: The Economic Consequences of the Peace (1919); A Treatise on Money (1930); The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936)
nodes.keyContribution: Aggregate demand determines output and employment
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: Richard Kahn, Joan Robinson, Austin Robinson, James Meade, Piero Sraffa; Student of: Alfred Marshall

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Deutscher Soziologe und Nationalökonom, bekannt für die These vom Zusammenhang zwischen protestantischer Ethik und Kapitalismus.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: German sociologist and political economist who founded modern sociology and analyzed the relationship between the Protestant ethic and capitalism.
nodes.keyWorks: The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism (1905); Economy and Society (1914); General Economic History (1923)
nodes.keyContribution: Protestant ethic's role in capitalism and the theory of Verstehen
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: Else von Richthofen; Student of: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Italienisch-britischer Ökonom, der Ricardos Theorie neu formulierte und die Cambridge-Kapitalkontroverse auslöste.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Italian-born economist who highlighted inconsistencies in Marshallian theory and solved Ricardo's theory for the moderns, inspiring the Classical Revival.
nodes.keyWorks: The Laws of Returns under Competitive Conditions (1926); Works and Correspondence of David Ricardo (1951); Production of Commodities by Means of Commodities (1960)
nodes.keyContribution: Solving Ricardo's theory and depicting the reswitching problem in capital theory
nodes.teacherStudent: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Deutscher Nationalökonom und Soziologe, Hauptvertreter der jüngeren Historischen Schule und Autor von „Der moderne Kapitalismus".
nodes.bioSummaryEn: A leading member of the last generation of the German Historical School, known for his work on modern capitalism and controversial political shifts.
nodes.keyWorks: Modern Capitalism (1902); The Jews and Modern Capitalism (1911); German Economy in the 19th Century (1903)
nodes.keyContribution: Modern Capitalism and the origins of capitalist acquisitiveness
nodes.teacherStudent: Student of: Schmoller, Wagner

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Österreichischer Ökonom, Begründer der Österreichischen Schule und der subjektiven Werttheorie.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Austrian economist who founded the Austrian School of thought and was one of the three leaders of the Marginalist Revolution of the 1870s.
nodes.keyWorks: Die Grundsätze der Volkswirthschaftslehre (1871); Untersuchungen über die Methode der Socialwissenschaften (1883); On the Origins of Money (1892)
nodes.keyContribution: Subjective theory of value and marginalist value theory
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk, Friedrich von Wieser, Crown Prince Rudolf, Karl Menger; Student of: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Britischer Philosoph und Ökonom, dessen „Principles of Political Economy" die klassische Theorie systematisch zusammenfassten.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: British philosopher, Classical economist, prophet of liberalism and public intellectual who restated Classical Ricardian theory.
nodes.keyWorks: Essays on Some Unsettled Questions of Political Economy (1844); Principles of Political Economy (1848); On Liberty (1859)
nodes.keyContribution: Restatement of the Classical Ricardian theory
nodes.teacherStudent: Student of: James Mill, Jeremy Bentham

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Britischer Ökonom, Schöpfer des IS-LM-Modells und Wegbereiter der neoklassisch-keynesianischen Synthese.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: One of the most important and influential economists of the twentieth century, known for his eclectic contributions to economic theory including the IS-LM model and Value and Capital.
nodes.keyWorks: Value and Capital (1939); Theory of Wages (1932); Capital and Growth (1965)
nodes.keyContribution: IS-LM model and Neo-Keynesian synthesis
nodes.teacherStudent: Student of: Lionel Robbins; Teacher of: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Schwedischer Ökonom, Begründer der Theorie des natürlichen Zinssatzes und des kumulativen Prozesses.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Swedish Neoclassical economist who pioneered the theory of the natural rate of interest and the cumulative process.
nodes.keyWorks: Value, Capital and Rent (1893); Interest and Prices (1898); Lectures on Political Economy (1901)
nodes.keyContribution: Natural rate of interest and the cumulative process
nodes.teacherStudent: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Deutscher Philosoph und Ökonom, dessen „Kapital" die Grundlage der marxistischen Wirtschaftstheorie bildet.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: German economist, philosopher and socialist revolutionary, founder of Marxian economics.
nodes.keyWorks: Communist Manifesto (1848); Das Kapital (1867)
nodes.keyContribution: Marxian economics and the theory of alienation
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: None found; Student of: Bruno Bauer

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Deutscher Nationalökonom, Begründer der älteren Historischen Schule der Nationalökonomie.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: German economist and historian who founded the older German Historical School and advocated for the historical method as a positive science.
nodes.keyWorks: Grundriss zu Vorlesungen über die Staatswirtschaft nach geschichtlichen Methode (1843); System der Volkswirtschaft (1854-94); Geschichte der National-oekonomik in Deutschland (1874)
nodes.keyContribution: Historical method as a positive science and cyclical stages theory of evolution
nodes.teacherStudent: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Schwedischer Ökonom, bekannt für seine Formalisierung der allgemeinen Gleichgewichtstheorie und die Kaufkraftparitätentheorie.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Swedish Neoclassical economist who formalized general equilibrium theory and introduced the purchasing power parity theory of exchange rates.
nodes.keyWorks: Theory of Social Economy (1918); The Nature and Necessity of Interest (1903); Money and Foreign Exchange after 1914 (1922)
nodes.keyContribution: Formalization of general equilibrium theory and purchasing power parity
nodes.teacherStudent: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Britischer Ökonom, Begründer der Theorie der komparativen Kostenvorteile und der klassischen Rententheorie.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: British economist who articulated the Classical system of political economy and developed the theory of comparative advantage.
nodes.keyWorks: The High Price of Bullion (1810); An Essay on the Influence of a Low Price of Corn on the Profits of Stock (1815); On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation (1817)
nodes.keyContribution: Classical system of political economy and comparative advantage
nodes.teacherStudent: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Amerikanischer Ökonom, Hauptvertreter des Monetarismus und der Chicagoer Schule.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: American economist who led the Monetarist incarnation of the Chicago School and advocated for free markets and laissez-faire economic policies.
nodes.keyWorks: A Theory of the Consumption Function (1957); A Monetary History of the United States, 1867-1960 (1963); Capitalism and Freedom (1962)
nodes.keyContribution: Monetarism and the Permanent Income Hypothesis
nodes.teacherStudent: Student of: Henry Schultz, Harold Hotelling, James Angell, Wesley Mitchell

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Deutscher Ökonom, Begründer des Ordoliberalismus und der Freiburger Schule, intellektueller Architekt der Sozialen Marktwirtschaft.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: German comparative economist trained in the tradition of the German Historical School who tried to synthesize their corporatist approach with Neoclassical theory.
nodes.keyWorks: Kapitaltheoretische Untersuchungen (1934); The Foundations of Economics (1940)
nodes.keyContribution: Synthesizing corporatist approach with Neoclassical theory and laissez-faire
nodes.teacherStudent: Student of: Heinrich Dietzel; Teacher of: Friedrich A. Lutz

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Österreichischer Ökonom, Begründer der österreichischen Kapitaltheorie und Lehrer einer ganzen Generation von Ökonomen.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Austrian economist, statesman, leading member of the Austrian School and creator of the Austrian theory of capital.
nodes.keyWorks: Capital und Capitalzins: Erste Abteilung, Geschichte und Kritik der Capitalstheorien (1884); Capital und Capitalzins: Zweite Abteilung, Positive Theorie des Capitals (1889)
nodes.keyContribution: Austrian theory of capital
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: Ludwig von Mises, Friedrich von Hayek, Joseph Schumpeter; Student of: Carl Menger

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Britischer Ökonom, Begründer der Wohlfahrtsökonomik und des Konzepts externer Effekte.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Cambridge Neoclassical economist who brought social welfare into economic analysis and pioneered the distinction between private and social costs.
nodes.keyWorks: Wealth and Welfare (1912); Economics of Welfare (1920); Theory of Unemployment (1933)
nodes.keyContribution: Brought social welfare into economic analysis and internalized externalities
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: None found; Student of: Alfred Marshall

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Deutscher Nationalökonom, Hauptvertreter der jüngeren Historischen Schule und Protagonist im Methodenstreit gegen Menger.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: German economist at the University of Berlin and paramount leader of the Younger German Historical School.
nodes.keyWorks: Zur Geschichte der deutschen Kleingewerbe im 19. Jahrhundert (1870); Umrisse (1898); Grundriss der allgemeinen Volkswirtschaftslehre (1900-04)
nodes.keyContribution: Methodenstreit and advocacy for historical/empirical analysis over abstract theory
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: his own students (via Staats- und Sozialwissenschaftliche Forschungen); Student of: None found

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Britischer Ökonom und Logiker, Mitbegründer der Marginalrevolution und der Grenznutzentheorie.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: English economist and logician who, simultaneously with Carl Menger and Léon Walras, launched the Marginalist Revolution of 1871-4.
nodes.keyWorks: The Coal Question (1865); The Theory of Political Economy (1871); Principles of Science (1874)
nodes.keyContribution: Marginalist Revolution and utility theory
nodes.teacherStudent: Student of: Augustus De Morgan

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Österreichisch-amerikanischer Ökonom, der die Theorie der komparativen Kosten in Opportunitätskosten reformulierte.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Austrian economic theorist who taught at Harvard and synthesized international trade and business cycle theories into rigorous encyclopaedic treatments.
nodes.keyWorks: Theory of International Trade (1936); Prosperity and Depression (1937)
nodes.keyContribution: Rewriting comparative advantage in terms of opportunity cost
nodes.teacherStudent: Teacher of: None found; Student of: Wieser, von Mises

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Österreichisch-amerikanischer Ökonom, Begründer der Praxeologie und radikaler Verfechter des Liberalismus.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: Eminence grise of the Austrian School who pioneered praxeology and the theory of human action.
nodes.keyWorks: The Theory of Money and Credit (1912); Socialism: An economic and sociological analysis (1922); Human Action: A treatise on economics (1949)
nodes.keyContribution: Praxeology and the theory of human action

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Britische Ökonomin der Cambridge-Schule, Pionierin der Theorie der unvollkommenen Konkurrenz.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: English economist who made fundamental contributions to the theory of imperfect competition, Keynesian economics, and the Cambridge Capital Controversy.
nodes.keyWorks: The Economics of Imperfect Competition (1933); An Essay on Marxian Economics (1942); The Accumulation of Capital (1956)
nodes.keyContribution: Theory of imperfect competition and capital aggregation in growth theory

nodes.bioSummaryDe: Deutscher Ökonom, intellektueller Wegbereiter der Sozialen Marktwirtschaft und des Ordoliberalismus.
nodes.bioSummaryEn: German economist and Ordo-liberal who helped establish the intellectual foundations for the post-war German social-market economy.
nodes.keyWorks: Economics in a Free Society (1937); The Social Crisis of our Time (1942); A Humane Economy (1958)
nodes.keyContribution: Intellectual foundations for the post-war German social-market economy

nodes.keyContribution: Austrian theory of capital
